_doc: Building footprints on Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35x for the 1904 target, one outline per building and per drawn part, keyed to the T-2982 sheet census. GENERATED by tools/trace_prairie_1904_footprints.py from the committed raster through the T-1250 fit -- do not hand-edit; re-run the tool. T-2982.
frame: local ENU metres of data/datum.json (x east, y north); polygon_px on the raster named above

method.classes: brick r-g>30 & r-b>25 & r>120; stone b-r>=10 & g>110; frame r-b>80 & g-b>60 & r>170 (8-bit sRGB); none where (r+g+b)/3<140, a drawn line on this coarse scan, its breaks of up to 3 px closed along rows and columns
method.assignment: the building nearest the street takes the frontage's front, attached and non_building_use census ids; the others take its detached_service ids nearest the alley first, and detached ids left over go onto the joined (several-part) outline nearest the alley; one left over on vacant ground takes that ground's id, any other is kept as unassigned. A frontage spanning several lots is read on their union

tiers.outline: inferred -- a 1911 survey carried to 1904 on T-2982's per-polygon ruling
tiers.part_role: inferred -- colour, size and position by the rule in each part's role_rule
tiers.storeys: not read here: the census's printed notation is the storey reading
tiers.for_1904: per building: as_mapped (the census rules it present in 1904 as drawn); not_1904 (a front the census backcasts from the 1886 plate -- the 1911 outline is a later replacement and no draft stands on it); as_mapped_rear_of_backcast (a rear building on a backcast frontage, drawn in 1911 and not ruled out); no_census_ruling

accuracy: the georeference's own fit residual (0.05 m RMS on its control crossings; the sheet's GCP file carries no independent check, so nothing better is claimed); the fit is a similarity at the printed scale on 2 degrees of freedom, so its residual says little about the sheet away from its crossings, plus about a pixel of trace (0.19 m on this coarser copy); relative accuracy inside one lot is the trace's, about 0.4 m
